headline: Lithium prices have sustainably recovered and the long-run price is expected to be structurally higher than consensus as demand from stationary energy storage and diesel replacement accelerates

quote: What was required to grow lithium raw material supply in the face of that emerging demand I've just described is a lot more raw material supply. The implication is that you pretty much needed 45% plus growth in lithium raw materials. To make that happen, costs go up because you go to lower grades, you go to areas that are harder to recover, typically more logistics, more remote. That all translates to higher cost and that's why the world is underestimating the average cost base in lithium raw material supply and that's why we can be a bit more confident about price.
